claims.head: The Canadiens should drive the play
claims.body: At 5-on-5, the Canadiens have been near the top of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Jets near the bottom. The ice should tilt the Canadiens’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 2 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Alex Iafallo takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4. Tyrel Bauer is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Fleury and Salomonsson.

Josh Morrissey is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 11 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Mario Ferraro has taken his spot beside Dylan DeMelo. That pair has had 47% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 89:53 together, down from 61% with Morrissey.
Nico Daws joined from NJD on Oct 24.
Dawson Mercer joined from NJD on Oct 24 and has played beside Kyle Connor and Viggo Björck.
Jack St. Ivany is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 4 games, down from 35% with his old team last season.
Elias Salomonsson has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 41% of the team’s power-play time in 5 games, up from 8% last season.

Nick Suzuki is out (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Oliver Kapanen has taken his spot beside Cole Caufield and Juraj Slafkovský. That line has had 51% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 30:10 together, down from 59% with Suzuki.
Ivan Demidov is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 12 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Mike Matheson is out two weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Lane Hutson has taken his spot beside Noah Dobson.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, down from 33% last season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 29% of the team’s shorthanded time in 13 games, up from 6% last season.

MTL.head: Advantage, the Canadiens
MTL.body: Even though Montréal will be without Suzuki, the Canadiens have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. On top of that, Winnipeg will be without Morrissey. The Jets can make it interesting if their power play gets going.

story.head: The Jets are desperate for a win
paras: The Jets are winless in nine (0-7-2). The Canadiens are on a tear, five straight wins. The Canadiens won the teams’ first meeting this season, 2-1 in Winnipeg on Oct 25. Going in, the Jets are seventh in the Central (tied for 27th in the NHL) and the Habs second in the Atlantic (fifth).

The Jets have played better than their record (.367) says: their chances are worth about .433, and their finishing has held them back. The Canadiens’ record (.714) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.567), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games.

The Jets create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (2nd) and rarely ice the puck (4th). They also take a lot of low-quality shots (30th), so the Canadiens wait for good looks, but them settle for hopeful ones. Winnipeg has scored 2.27 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. On the other side, the Canadiens get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (5th), but take more penalties than they draw (32nd). The Canadiens are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Jets.

Kyle Connor (11 G / 4 A / 15 P in 15 GP) leads the Jets in scoring, with five goals in six games against Montréal since 2023-24. Mark Scheifele (2 G / 10 A / 12 P in 15 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Canadiens, Lane Hutson (3 G / 10 A / 13 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Cole Caufield (8 G / 4 A / 12 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Stuart Skinner (3-4-3 / .887 SV% in 10 GS) is in line to start for Winnipeg. Jacob Fowler (7-1-0 / .932 SV% in 8 GS) has been a rock in net for Montréal and will likely start.
The Canadiens usually control more of the chances than the Jets do.
